messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@trumed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Dedicated capacity for TruMed - SLO targets & throughput clarifications

Jordan — thanks for the demo today. Quick recap and a few clarifying points so we can align on sizing for a dedicated pilot. High level: we need a predictable serving configuration for inference that meets clinical UI SLAs.

Quick context: TruMed will use a 6–8 turn conversational model for clinician note assist (typical prompt 40–120 input tokens, 30–200 reply tokens). Latency is critical for usability in the EHR.

Key asks we discussed on the call:
- Target p95 latency <= 150ms for generation (streaming enabled) on short responses (~<=128 tokens).
- Sustained throughput: 10 qps baseline, with sustained concurrency ~50 simultaneous sessions.
- Burst capability to 70–90 qps for 10–30s during shift changes.
- Throughput must be predictable (no big variance) — want to size reserved throughput accordingly.

Questions for you to confirm in a short follow-up:
1) From Redwood’s perspective, what reserved pool (GPU type + count) would you recommend to meet p95 150ms target with 10 qps sustained and burst headroom?
2) Any tradeoffs if we prefer cost control (cheaper GPUs + quantization) vs straight H100 deployments?
3) How will streaming + KV/prefix caching change the sizing?

If you can send a short mutual action plan and proposed pilot config we can review with procurement this week. Attaching our internal SLO spreadsheet for your reference.

Appreciate it —
Alice
Alice Chen
Head of ML Platforms, TruMed
alice@trumed.com

Attachment: TruMed_SLO_summary.xlsx (workbook — SLO targets & session profile)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@trumed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Dedicated capacity for TruMed - SLO targets & throughput clarifications

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear notes and the SLO workbook. Saw a few items that help us size: average response length and session concurrency distribution. I’m putting a short pilot proposal below plus a few clarifying Qs.

High-level pilot proposal (first-cut):
- Pilot objective: validate p95 <= 150ms for <=128 token responses with streaming and measure sustained 10 qps baseline + burst to 90 qps.
- Recommended reserved pool (initial): 3x H100 (reserved) with auto-burst to 6x H100 for predictable headroom.
  - Why H100: better kernel throughput for FP16/AMP models we saw in the demo; reduces tail latency for streaming.
- Cost-sensitive alternative: 6x A100 (or 4x A10G mixed) with aggressive KV/prefix caching and quantization — lower monthly cost but higher risk of p95 regression.

Sizing assumptions I used:
- Model family: medium LLM (~12–14B equivalent in throughput profile)
- Typical generation length for SLO target: 100 tokens out (p95 target window)
- Measured tokens/sec per H100 under streaming test: ~650–850 tokens/sec depending on batch and concurrency (see attached bench CSV).

Clarifying questions to ensure we match your workload:
1) Do you have a hard upper bound on latency for longer responses (>256 tokens)? We only need baseline for pilot shorter-path SLOs.
2) Any regulatory constraints on outbound telemetry (we can run pilot inside VPC if needed)?
3) Who will own the mutual action plan sign-off on your side (procurement or platform)?

I attached a short PDF with the back-of-envelope sizing and the CSV of microbench kernels. Karthik/Ben — adding you for sizing confirmation and any ops caveats.

Next steps proposed:
1) Jordan and team share sizing workbook + estimated monthly cost (today) — target Monday.
2) TruMed to confirm pilot scope + preferred region and compliance needs.
3) Set a 60–90 minute pilot kickoff with infra and TruMed platform owners — propose Tue/Wed window.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-slo-sizing-estimates.pdf, kernel-latency-bench.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: Dedicated capacity for TruMed - SLO targets & throughput clarifications

Jordan — quick internal note on the numbers after running the microbench overnight. Keep this internal until we vet with Alice.

Short takeaways:
- H100 profile: ~1.6x tokens/sec vs A100 for the trimmed model. Tail latencies (99th) are ~25–40% better on H100 in our streaming kernel path because of faster attention kernels. That directly impacts p95.
- Concurrency model: one H100 can sustain ~12 concurrent streaming sessions at p95 150ms for ~100 token outputs when we enable continuous batching + KV cache for common prefixes. Without KV caching, concurrency drops to ~7 sessions.
- Reserve math for 10 qps sustained (50 concurrent sessions):
  - If each session averages 0.2 qps (given think-time, per-user interactions), you need concurrency headroom ~50. At 12 sessions per H100, baseline = 5 H100 to meet concurrency without caching. With prefix caching in place, baseline drops to ~3 H100.
- Burst sizing: to cover 90 qps short bursts we should have autoscale to 7–8 H100 or allow cross-region fallback to an additional pool for burst absorb.

Suggested pilot config (internal):
- Reserved: 3 H100 with KV/prefix cache enabled, request 24/7 autoscale policy to +3 H100 on 95th percentile queueing threshold.
- Observability: per-token latency traces, per-route token counters, and p95 alerting.
- Acceptance criteria: sustained 10 qps with p95 <=150ms for <=128 tokens, no more than 3 incidents in a 72-hour run.

I’ll drop the microbench CSV in the drive link (see thread metadata) and a short Jupyter that computes the reserve math if anyone wants to iterate.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: Dedicated capacity for TruMed - SLO targets & throughput clarifications

Karthik — good notes. Two practical additions from a procurement/ops perspective:
- Cost balance: if TruMed requires a long-running reserved pool, propose a mixed fleet pilot: 2x H100 (reserved) + 2x A10G (reserved) and autoscale additional H100 during burst windows. This reduces committed spend while letting us validate H100 tail behavior.
- Quantization caveat: aggressive 4-bit quant will reduce memory and may increase tokens/sec, but we should only use that for non-critical paths (e.g., draft generation) until we validate hallucination/regression risk.

My suggested customer-facing pilot pitch:
1) Start with 3-week pilot using 3x reserved H100 (KV caching enabled).
2) During week 2 run a cost experiment: route 20% of traffic to mixed fleet (A10 + quantized) to measure p95 impact.
3) Final week: decision review and sizing adjustment for production commit.

I’ll prepare a short cost delta slide for Monday.

—Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Alice — looping back with a concise mutual action plan and our recommended pilot configuration. CC’ing Karthik and Ben so they’re visible on ops and commercial items.

Mutual action plan (proposed)
- Scope: validate p95 <= 150ms for <=128 token streaming responses, measure sustained 10 qps baseline, and test burst to 90 qps.
- Initial reserved pool: 3x H100 (reserved) in us-west-2; autoscale policy to +3 H100 on queueing threshold; KV/prefix caching enabled.
- Cost experiment (week 2 of pilot): route 20% of traffic to a mixed fleet (2x A10G) with quantization to evaluate cost/perf tradeoffs.
- Observability & acceptance: per-route p95/p99, token counters, and 4-hr postmortem for any incident. Acceptance: 72-hr continuous run with p95 <=150ms and no more than 3 SLO breaches.
- Timeline:
  - Tue 6/9: Procurement confirms pilot PO/region and security constraints.
  - Wed 6/10: Pilot kickoff (60–90m) — infra + TruMed platform owners.
  - Wed-Fri 6/10–6/12: Smoke tests + baseline runs.
  - Week 2: cost experiment and mixed-fleet routing.
  - Week 3: decision review and production sizing recommendation.

Action items for TruMed: confirm pilot scope and PO contact; share preferred region and any VPC/KMS constraints; nominate platform owner for the kickoff.
Action items for Redwood: share a detailed sizing workbook (attached) and a formal cost delta slide; provision pilot reserved pool once PO is in place.

I’ve attached the sizing PDF and the kernel bench CSV again. If that timeline works I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed morning.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.
